title: Directed graphs, paths, cycles, and Hasse diagrams
proposed_reference_coverage: **Directed graphs: paths, reachability, cycles, and Hasse diagrams**
fact_or_context_to_reference: Relations are directed edges: positive-length paths give transitive closure, paths allowing length zero give reflexive-transitive closure, and paths allowing either edge orientation give the equivalence closure and connected-component partition. The cover graph of a finite poset recovers strict comparison by upward paths; covers alone do not recover arbitrary infinite or dense orders. Acyclicity of a finite relation implies well-foundedness, but an acyclic infinite relation need not be well-founded. Foundation excludes every positive finite membership cycle. The three-point path illustrates that an acyclic extensional relation need not be transitive. Provide the general directed-path, strongly connected component quotient, finite topological-order and cycle-deletion results behind the specialized implication-graph constructions in 2-SAT, with their broader graph-theory context.
